Case law verified against fetched published opinions; items marked 'cite_confirmed_quote_pending' have a confirmed reporter cite but the verbatim quote/pinpoint should be pulled from the bound reporter before quoting. Lines without cases are statute/reg-only by design (mechanical computations). [VERIFY] notes flag items for Taylor's professional confirmation. No Westlaw/Lexis used.

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Bucklin, 70 Wn. App. 837, 855 P.2d 1197 (Div. 1 1993)
cases.parenthetical: self-employed obligor's income must reflect all sources; an obligor who fails to produce adequate records cannot benefit from the resulting uncertainty

lines.label: Other Income
rcw: RCW 26.19.071(3) (remaining enumerated categories (c)-(t), e.g., commissions, overtime, bonuses, pensions, social security, workers' comp, unemployment)
lines.note: Excluded categories are listed in RCW 26.19.071(4) (new-spouse income, child support from other relationships, gifts/prizes, TANF, SSI, ABD, food stamps, debt-retirement overtime/2nd-job).

lines.label: Imputed Income

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Peterson, 80 Wn. App. 148, 906 P.2d 1009 (Div. 1 1995), review denied, 129 Wn.2d 1014 (1996)
cases.parenthetical: income may not be imputed to a parent gainfully employed full time absent a finding the parent is purposely underemployed to reduce the support obligation; defining 'gainfully employed'

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Schumacher, 100 Wn. App. 208, 997 P.2d 399 (Div. 1 2000)
cases.parenthetical: 'full time' is not fixed at 40 hours; the hours customary for the parent's occupation control

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Goodell, 130 Wn. App. 381, 122 P.3d 929 (Div. 2 2005)
cases.parenthetical: RCW 26.19.071(6) governs imputation; trial court erred in failing to impute income to a voluntarily underemployed parent

lines.note: Six-tier imputation order in RCW 26.19.071(6)(a)(i)-(vi); full-time-student rule (6)(b). INCARCERATION imputation: now addressed by statute (EHB 1014 abatement to $10/mo for 6+ months' incarceration); [VERIFY: no published WA case located this pass — Taylor to confirm if a case pick is wanted].

lines.label: Income Taxes (Federal and State)
lines.note: Washington has no state income tax; state component = $0 for WA residents. Worksheet takes the parent's actual/disclosed tax (no embedded estimator).

lines.label: Mandatory State Deductions (state insurance premiums incl. PFML and WA Cares / long-term services & supports trust)
lines.note: NEW line under EHB 1014 (Laws 2025 ch. 272), effective 1/1/2026. Re-letters the rest of subsection (5).

lines.label: Voluntary Retirement Contributions
lines.note: Capped at up to $5,000/yr; was (5)(g) before 2026.

lines.label: Maintenance Paid
lines.note: Court-ordered maintenance to the extent actually paid; was (5)(f) before 2026.

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Bucklin, 70 Wn. App. 837, 855 P.2d 1197 (Div. 1 1993)
cases.parenthetical: self-employed obligor's income must reflect all sources; an obligor who fails to produce adequate records cannot benefit from the resulting uncertainty

lines.label: Basic Child Support Obligation (per child from the economic table x number of children)

cases.cite: In re Marriage of McCausland, 159 Wn.2d 607, 152 P.3d 1013 (2007) (en banc)
cases.parenthetical: a court may exceed the economic table only on written findings of fact and may NOT mechanically extrapolate; must at minimum consider the Daubert/Rusch factors. NOTE: decided under the former $5,000/$7,000 thresholds; the no-extrapolation / written-findings holding remains good law for amounts above the current $50,000 ceiling, but McCausland's dollar figures are superseded by EHB 1014 (2026)

cases.cite: State ex rel. M.M.G. v. Graham, 159 Wn.2d 623, 152 P.3d 1005 (2007)
cases.parenthetical: companion case to McCausland; a court must enter written findings of fact supporting any decision to exceed the economic table / any deviation or its denial

lines.note: Economic table is PER CHILD; total = per-child x N. Presumptive to $50,000 combined net (RCW 26.19.065(3)); above that, written findings required (McCausland/Graham), no mechanical extrapolation.

lines.label: Each Parent's Basic Child Support Obligation (without low-income limitations)
Self-Support Reserve (180% of the federal poverty guideline, one-person)
lines.note: Raised 125%->180% by EHB 1014 (2026). [VERIFY: no published WA case located on the reserve mechanic this pass; the figure is statutory.]

lines.label: Parent's net income < self-support reserve -> presumptive $50 per child
Parent's net income >= self-support reserve -> subtract reserve (not below it), floor $50/child
Any other biological or legal children (whole-family / other-relationship)

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Bell, 101 Wn. App. 366, 4 P.3d 849 (Div. 1 2000)
cases.parenthetical: deviation for children from other relationships must rest on the total circumstances of both households; 'child support is not a first-come, first-served proposition'

lines.label: Each parent's basic support obligation after limitations (not less than $50/child)
Monthly Health Insurance Premiums Paid for Child(ren)
lines.note: Health care shared in proportion to the basic obligation (26.19.080(2)). Reasonable-cost limit on required coverage = 25% of the parent's basic support obligation (RCW 26.09.105; see line 19).

lines.label: Uninsured Monthly Health Care Expenses Paid for Child(ren)
Day Care Expenses
lines.note: Day care/special expenses shared proportionally; 20%-overpayment reimbursement mechanic in (3); court discretion as to necessity/reasonableness (4).

lines.label: Total Day Care and Special Expenses
Combined Monthly Total Day Care and Special Expenses
Total Health Care, Day Care, and Special Expenses
Each Parent's Obligation for Health Care, Day Care, and Special Expenses
Child Support Credits (health care / day care & special / other ordinary expenses credit; total)
lines.note: Credits a parent for add-on amounts that parent pays directly, so the transfer payment is net. [VERIFY: exact RCW subsection for the credit mechanic vs. AOC worksheet instructions.]

lines.label: Standard Calculation / Presumptive Transfer Payment
lines.note: The standard calculation is presumptive; the court must order it unless written findings support a deviation (RCW 26.19.075(2),(3)). Agreement of the parties alone is not adequate reason to deviate (RCW 26.19.075(5)).

lines.label: 45% of each parent's net income (informational limit)
25% of each parent's basic support obligation (informational; health-coverage reasonable-cost ceiling)
lines.note: Required health-coverage cost is 'reasonable' / can be ordered if it does not exceed 25% of the parent's basic support obligation (RCW 26.09.105). [VERIFY: exact subsection of 26.09.105 for the 25% figure.]

lines.label: Household Assets (additional factors for consideration)
lines.note: Deviation factors: sources of income/tax planning (1)(a); debt and high expenses (1)(c).

lines.label: Other factors: income of children / income from child support / income from assistance programs / other income
Deviation — residential schedule (significant time with the obligor parent)

cases.cite: State ex rel. M.M.G. v. Graham, 159 Wn.2d 623, 152 P.3d 1005 (2007)
cases.parenthetical: companion case to McCausland; a court must enter written findings of fact supporting any decision to exceed the economic table / any deviation or its denial

lines.note: Discretionary, NOT a formula; barred where it leaves the receiving household short of the child's basic needs or the child receives TANF (statutory). Graham supplies the written-findings requirement. [VERIFY: a residential-schedule-specific published holding was not confirmed this pass — Taylor may add one.]

lines.label: Postsecondary educational support (separate from basic support)

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Newell, 117 Wn. App. 711, 72 P.3d 1130 (Div. 1 2003)
cases.parenthetical: postsecondary educational support is discretionary; the schedule is advisory, not mandatory, for postsecondary support (RCW 26.19.090); income/proportional shares must still be computed first

cases.cite: In re Marriage of Kelly, 85 Wn. App. 785, 934 P.2d 1218 (Div. 1 1997)
cases.parenthetical: postsecondary educational support lies within the trial court's discretion (relied on in Newell)

lines.label: Worksheet certification / signatures
lines.note: Worksheets completed under penalty of perjury and filed in every proceeding; AOC develops the worksheets/instructions (RCW 26.19.050).
